evidence.source: Mace et al. 2018, ApJ 854, 145 (2018ApJ...854..145M), sections 1, 4.1-4.3 and Table 3
evidence.scope: Completes the corrected CNS5 GJ 781 pair in place. Mace et al. label the sdM primary A, the unseen white dwarf B (WD 2003+542) and the T8 subdwarf C. The frozen SIMBAD main identifier Wolf 1130 B for CNS5 4977 is the earlier name of C and remains one of its designations. The A-B orbit (P = 0.49670418 +/- 0.00000005 d, i = 29 +/- 2 deg, a = 0.014183 au) is not modelled.

components.label: A
components.note: Wolf 1130 A is the exact CNS5 4975 / SIMBAD Wolf 1130 record, which observes the A+B spectroscopic binary. B contributes no detected visible or near-infrared light (Mace et al. 2018, section 4.2), so existing photometry, astrometry and spectrum describe A; existing measurements retained. Its Gaia DR3 radial velocity (7.3 +/- 23.9 km/s) is blurred by A's 121 km/s orbital semi-amplitude; the published systemic velocity is -33.2 km/s (Table 3).

components.label: B
components.note: Wolf 1130 B is the unseen white dwarf in a 0.4967-day orbit with A, detected only through A's radial velocities and ellipsoidal light variation (Mace et al. 2018, sections 3.2 and 4.2). Shared A position and distance; separation 0.014 au. Non-detection implies Teff below 7000 K and a cooling age above about 3.4 Gyr; no spectral type, temperature, photometry or space motion is available.

components.label: C
components.note: Wolf 1130 C is the exact CNS5 4977 T8 subdwarf, a common-proper-motion companion at a projected 3150 +/- 40 au (Mace et al. 2018, section 4.3 and Table 5). Its own astrometry is retained.
